previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fatigue, malaise, low-grade fever, and loose stools. He has a history of HCV cirrhosis with ascites, portopulmonary hypertension on remodulin, and recent tunneled line replacement. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis and stable bilateral lower lobe opacities on chest X-ray, but no focal infection source. Stool studies were negative for C. difficile, Salmonella, Shigella, and Campylobacter. Paracentesis showed minimal PMNs, ruling out spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. Blood cultures remained negative. His symptoms improved without antibiotics, supporting a viral gastroenteritis diagnosis. He underwent therapeutic paracentesis to remove 8 liters of ascites after platelet transfusion due to thrombocytopenia, with symptomatic relief. All home medications, including remodulin, were continued. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor weight and follow up with his transplant team.

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Cirrhosis, central line placement.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous radiograph, the patient has received a
right-sided central venous access line.  The tip of the line projects over the
mid to lower SVC.  The Dobbhoff catheter is unchanged, the tip cannot be
reliably visualized.  The pre-existing parenchymal opacities at the lung bases
have almost completely resolved.  The size of the cardiac silhouette is
unchanged.  There is no evidence of pneumothorax.

INDICATION:  HCV cirrhosis.  Evaluate for placement of Dobbhoff tube.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal radiograph ___.

FINDINGS:  Single portable supine frontal radiograph of the abdomen reveals a
nonspecific bowel gas pattern without dilated loops.  An enteric tube coils
one and half times in the stomach with its tip terminating in the body of the
stomach.  There is surgical hardware and evidence of vertebroplasties in the
lower lumbar spine.  Surgical clips project over the right upper quadrant. 
There is a partially visualized catheter projecting over the right lower
hemithorax; however, without an orthogonal view, it is unclear whether this is
internal or external to the patient.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Dobbhoff tube coils with its tip terminating in the stomach.
2.  Nonspecific bowel gas pattern without dilated loops of bowel.

HISTORY:  Ascites.  

PROCEDURE/FINDINGS:

Prior to the start of the procedure, written informed consent was obtained
from the patient.  A preprocedural timeout was performed as per departmental
protocol. An appropriate site for paracentesis was selected under ultrasound
guidance along the left lower abdominal quadrant.  The patient was then
prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  The skin was anesthetized
with 1% lidocaine solution.  A 5 ___ ___ catheter was advanced into the
peritoneal cavity, following which a 7.6 L of clear yellow-orange ascitic
fluid was drained.  The catheter was then removed and a single suture was used
to close the puncture site.  A sterile dressing was then applied.  The patient
tolerated the procedure well, without immediate complication. 

The attending radiologist, Dr. ___, was present during the critical portions
of the procedure.  

IMPRESSION:

Technically successful ultrasound-guided therapeutic paracentesis, yielding
7.6 L of clear ascitic fluid.

HISTORY:  Left greater than right lower extremity swelling.  Evaluate for DVT
in the left leg.

COMPARISON:  Lower extremity ultrasound on ___.

FINDINGS:

There is normal phasicity and response to Valsalva manuever in the common
femoral veins bilaterally.  There is normal compression, augmentation and flow
of the common femoral, superficial femoral, popliteal, peroneal, and posterior
tibial veins of the left leg.  Subcutaneous edema is seen in the mid and
distal calf.

IMPRESSION:

No evidence of DVT in the left leg.
